  WHY: If digest writing fails while the item already has `ai:needs-human`, the label and marker remain and the scan skips the item permanently without a digest entry.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 496-514 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Creating the digest is a check-then-create sequence with no concurrency protection or post-create reconciliation.
  WHY: Two concurrent park calls can both create a digest, while later calls and pruning select only the oldest matching digest, leaving entries in the other digest out of subsequent updates and pruning and breaking the requirement for one digest per repository.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 497-501 and 537-540 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the digest issue disappears from the open-issue listing after a PATCH succeeds (e.g. a human closes or unlabels it between loop iterations), the `break` on line 501 exits the convergence loop without raising `ApiError`, and lines 537-540 return `newly_parked=True` with `issue=None`.
  WHY: The caller (`needs_human_park` or the judge `needs_human` handler) receives `newly_parked=True` and sends a CRITICAL alert naming the digest issue number (or "?" when issue is None). No digest entry was actually written. The item retains `ai:needs-human` without a corresponding digest line, and the scan skips it as parked without any entry for a person to find.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 475-488 in `needs_human_park` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The label rollback on digest-write failure (lines 480-487) deletes `ai:needs-human` whenever `--item-labeled` was omitted, regardless of whether the label existed before this call added it.
  WHY: The poller's `needs_human_park_project` (with `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_ENABLED=false`) always omits `--item-labeled`. If the tracking issue already carries `ai:needs-human` from a human latch (e.g., a prior `ai:needs-human` added by a person, distinct from the staged-support marker), the label POST is a no-op, and a digest-write failure in `_needs_human_park_digest` then deletes the pre-existing human gate.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh (lines 790-795) and scripts/unblock_scan.py (lines 249-255) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: For a needs-human digest park, the judge records the verdict comment (with `verdict=close`) BEFORE running the `needs_human` operation. If the `needs_human` op fails with `--item-labeled` (the item already carried `ai:needs-human`), the label is not rolled back, but no digest entry was written.
  WHY: The verdict comment is the durable record the scan uses to decide "parked." The digest operation is an impermanent side effect. When it fails after the verdict is committed, the item enters a state the scan treats as parked but has no digest entry. No retry occurs because the scan skips immediately, and the verdict marker's round counter was already spent.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: _needs_human_park_digest, lines 491-540 (loop body at 496-534; specifically the `if digest is None: if wrote: break` branch at 497-501) | confidence=4 | severity=MAJOR
  PROBLEM: When a digest PATCH succeeds on iteration N but the verification `_list_digest` on iteration N+1 returns None (digest was closed, had its label removed, or fell out of the open-issue listing), the loop breaks and falls through to a "successful" return with `newly_parked=True` and `issue=None`.
  WHY: A digest closed between PATCH and verification (or even an interrupted attempt that left the listing stale) leaves a labelled item the scan will never re-judge. The CRITICAL alert the caller sends will read `in needs-human digest #?`, which makes the failure visible to an operator but does not unstick the item.
- needs_human_park, lines 475-488 (the new try/except rollback added in this last run) | confidence=4 | severity=MAJOR
  PROBLEM: The rollback at lines 481-487 deletes `ai:needs-human` whenever `--item-labeled` is false, without checking whether the label was already on the item before this call.
  WHY: The poller caller in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17012-17015` deliberately omits `--item-labeled`, so any project that already has `ai:needs-human` for a reason outside this code path loses its gate on the next transient digest write failure (network blip, rate-limit, JSON parse error of the digest listing).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh
  Line or code reference: verdict comment POST at line 792, followed by ops execution at line 803, with the `needs_human` op handled at lines 349-366
  PROBLEM: The judge records the verdict marker (including `verdict=close`) on the item's comments at line 792 BEFORE running the ops file, and `operator_step_issue.py needs-human park` is one of those ops at line 358. When the item already has `ai:needs-human` (so `--item-labeled` is set at line 356), a digest write failure (network error, JSON parse, listing lag) means no rollback fires (the rollback branch is gated on `not item_labeled`), but the close verdict marker is already on the issue. On the next scan tick, `scripts/unblock_scan.py:249-256` sees `ai:needs-human` plus a `close` verdict and skips the item as `parked` indefinitely.
  WHY: The verdict-before-actuation ordering is intentional ("The ledger record goes first, so a failed operation below can never make the same verdict available again") but the last run's rollback intentionally leaves the label alone when `--item-labeled` is set, so the combination strands any item where the digest write fails after the verdict has been recorded. The kill switch `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false` lets such items reach the judge again, but a transient digest failure under the default `true` is permanent.
